$comment: Design language, not cars. Every entry describes an era, a set of constraints that produced a
shape, and real proportions in metres — the things that actually steer a generator — plus an
`avoid` list naming what must not appear. Nothing here names a marque, a model or a team: a
prompt that names one gets a copy of that one, which is the outcome this file exists to prevent.
See README.md for why each field is shaped the way it is.

defaults.background: flat chroma-green #2ecc40, evenly lit, no gradient, no shadow on the backdrop
defaults.camera: level with the subject's mid-height, no perspective distortion, subject fully in frame with a small margin
defaults.render: clean studio product render, neutral daylight, matte finish, no motion blur, no lens flare, no text
avoid: manufacturer badges, marque emblems, grille crests or wordmarks of any kind
real sponsor marks, oil-company colours, cigarette-brand liveries
model names or type numbers anywhere on the body
licence plates bearing real jurisdictions
watermarks, signatures, captions, UI, borders

silhouette: Mid-engined two-seat closed coupe. The cabin sits forward of centre and the mass is behind it:
roughly a third of the length ahead of the windscreen, two-thirds behind.
Height barely above a metre, so the roof is at the level of a standing adult's hip.
cues: low, wide, rounded nose with a full-width air intake slot beneath a soft leading edge
separate raised fender crowns over each front wheel, higher than the bonnet between them, so the driver can place the car
a bonnet valley running between those crowns, with two NACA-style flush ducts
steeply raked one-piece wraparound windscreen meeting a very short roof
flying buttresses running back from the roof to the rear fenders, leaving a recessed rear window
large half-moon cutouts over the rear wheels for tyre clearance and heat
a full-width horizontal spoiler lip at the tail, no upright fin, no high wing
exposed exhaust primaries emerging under the tail panel
wide slotted magnesium wheels, deeply dished, five-spoke, with knock-off centre nuts
a shallow chin spoiler under the nose
materials: hand-laid painted fibreglass with slight surface undulation, not machine-flat
clear-taped headlamp covers faired into the nose
bare riveted aluminium around the exhaust exits
plain dark rubber tyres with a faint period block tread
avoid: a pointed wedge nose or chisel front — that is a decade too late
a tall upright tail fin or swan-neck wing
modern low-profile tyres, alloy multi-spoke wheels, LED lamps
roll hoop protruding above the roofline
any racing number or roundel; liveries are applied separately

assets.era: early-1970s mass-market full-size saloon, North American market
silhouette: Three-box saloon, long bonnet, upright cabin, flat boot. Body sits high on its wheels with visible gap over the tyre.
cues: flat horizontal bonnet meeting a full-width grille of fine vertical bars
stacked or paired round headlamps at the outer corners
thin chrome bumper standing clear of the body on visible overriders
square-shouldered body sides with a single crisp crease along the length
thin-pillared six-light glasshouse, near-vertical rear screen
modest tailfin residue: a raised edge along the rear wing, not a fin
steel wheels with small chrome hubcaps and whitewall tyres
materials: single-stage enamel in a muted period colour
bright chrome brightwork
painted steel wheels
avoid: any modern shape: no wedge, no fastback, no blacked-out pillars
aerodynamic mirrors
alloy wheels

silhouette: Two-box: upright cab forward, open cargo bed behind, straight beltline running the whole length.
cues: flat slab sides with a step behind the cab
wide simple grille, single round headlamps either side
painted steel front bumper, no overriders
small wrap-around rear window in the cab
external fuel filler on the rear wing
plain steel wheels, chunky sidewalls
materials: work-grade paint with honest wear, chalked on the horizontal surfaces
a dusty matte finish, never showroom
avoid: crew cab, four doors, lifted suspension, modern grille

silhouette: One box. The windscreen is almost directly above the front axle; the nose barely exists.
cues: near-vertical flat windscreen
sliding side door with a recessed track
unglazed rear panels
small round headlamps low on the flat front
roof gutters running the full length
materials: flat single colour with a hand-painted blank signwriting panel on the flank, lettering left off
avoid: modern high-roof profile, body-coloured bumpers, tinted glass

silhouette: Long bonnet, short deck, fastback roof falling in one line from the windscreen to the tail.
cues: bonnet bulge or scoop
recessed grille with hidden or deeply set lamps
muscular haunch over the rear wheel
short ducktail lip on the boot
wide steel wheels with trim rings
materials: saturated period colour
matte black bonnet stripe or blackout panel
avoid: spoilers beyond a small lip, side skirts, modern tyres

silhouette: A bare slender trunk with a slight lean, and a crown only at the very top.
cues: trunk visibly ringed with old frond scars, thicker at the base
nine to twelve fronds, the upper ones arcing up, the lower ones drooping past horizontal
a short skirt of dead brown fronds under the green crown
no branches anywhere on the trunk
materials: dry fibrous grey-brown trunk
fronds in a dusty desaturated green, sun-bleached at the tips
avoid: a symmetrical lollipop crown
a smooth cylindrical trunk
any visible pot, base disc or ground plane

silhouette: Two storeys, long and low, rooms in a row, an external walkway running the full length of the upper floor.
cues: cantilevered upper walkway with a thin steel balustrade of repeated vertical rods
a door and a single window per room, evenly repeated
a butterfly or shallow-pitched roof with a deep overhang
a projecting office block at one end, fully glazed
exposed breeze-block screen wall at the stair end
ice machine and a soft-drink cooler recessed by the stair
materials: painted stucco in a pale colour
turquoise or coral trim on the doors
aggregate concrete walkway
avoid: any readable brand name
modern glazing, uPVC, or a flat parapet

silhouette: A tall thin sign on a single steel pole, far taller than the building it serves.
cues: a boomerang or starburst crown above a rectangular message panel
an arrow of chase lamps along the lower edge
exposed neon tubing standing off the face on visible spacers
a small changeable-letter panel beneath the main field
a plain riveted steel pole with a visible splice
materials: enamelled steel face
glass neon in two colours
unpainted galvanised pole
avoid: any actual brand, chain or slogan — leave every lettering panel BLANK; wording is applied later
LED panels, modern typography, backlit acrylic

silhouette: A small glazed box with a large flat canopy reaching out over the forecourt on slender columns.
cues: flat canopy with a deep fascia band, thin round columns
two pump islands under it, each with a pair of tall narrow pumps
a fully glazed sales office on one side
one open service bay with a folding door
a hose-and-bell across the forecourt approach
materials: white porcelain-enamel panels
a single accent colour on the fascia
oil-stained concrete forecourt
avoid: brand marks on the fascia or pumps — leave them blank
modern pump displays, canopy downlights, convenience store

silhouette: A lattice truss spanning the road on two legs, with blank sign panels hung beneath it.
cues: galvanised tube lattice with visible bolted gussets
two blank rectangular panels hung on the truss
a maintenance walkway along the back
a pair of downlights per panel
materials: galvanised steel gone chalky
plain reflective sheeting on the blank panels
avoid: any legible destination text or route shield
modern variable-message display
